title: High-degree comparison for a punctured-spectrum perverse upper bound
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and $X$ a Noetherian excellent normal strictly henselian local scheme of dimension $d\geq2$, with closed point $x$ and $\ell$ invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Put $U=X-\{x\}$ and $\varphi(y)=\max(0,2\dim\mathcal O_{X,y}-2)$ for $y\in U$. Let $M\in D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Assume that $H^a(M|_{\bar y})=0$ for every geometric point over $y$ and $a>\varphi(y)$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and that a specified isomorphism $\alpha:\Lambda_U\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau^{\mathrm{ord}}_{\leq0}M$ is given. Let $u:\Lambda_U\to M$ be its composite with the ordinary truncation map. Then for every $q\geq2d$ the map
$$H^{q-1}(U,\Lambda)\xrightarrow{H^{q-1}(u)}H^{q-1}(U,M)$$
is an isomorphism. Here the groups are etale hypercohomology, computed by derived global sections [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 5.3.2 (printed pp. 288–289), using Proposition 3.2.1 and hypercohomology; no finite-type-over-field assumption

proof.text:
Work with the underlying abelian etale complexes when computing hypercohomology. Set $C=\tau^{\mathrm{ord}}_{\geq1}M$. The ordinary truncation triangle, after identifying its first term with $\Lambda_U$ by the specified $\alpha$, is
$$\Lambda_U\xrightarrow{u}M\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow\Lambda_U[1].$$
The truncation formulas give $\mathcal H^r(C)=0$ for $r\leq0$ and $\mathcal H^r(C)=\mathcal H^r(M)$ for $r\geq1$. These are sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules, in particular killed by $\ell^n$. The first arrow is exactly the map in the statement, since it is the composite of $\alpha$ with the truncation map.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 5.3.2, printed pp. 288–289; Proposition 3.2.1, printed p. 268

proof.text:
Write $h_y=\dim\mathcal O_{X,y}$ and $e_y=\dim\overline{\{y\}}$, the latter closure being in $X$. The generalization-chain description of $h_y$ and the Krull-dimension definition imply
$$h_y\leq d-1\quad(y\in U),\qquad h_y+e_y\leq d.$$
For the first inequality, append the proper specialization $y\rightsquigarrow x$ to a chain of generalizations of $y$; for the second concatenate a chain from a generalization to $y$ with a chain in its closure starting at $y$. In finite dimension the finite integer suprema are attained; a chain in the irreducible closure may be extended to start at its generic point $y$. Both concatenations are chains in $X$, so their length is at most $d$. Exactness of geometric stalks identifies $(\mathcal H^rM)_{\bar y}$ with $H^r(M|_{\bar y})$. Thus the assumed stalk bound, $h_y\leq d-1$, and stalk conservativity give $\mathcal H^r(C)=0$ for $r>2d-4$. In dimension $2$ this and Step 1 make every cohomology sheaf of $C$ zero, so $C=0$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 5.3.2, printed pp. 288–289; Proposition 3.2.1, printed p. 268

proof.text:
For $1\leq i\leq d-2$, set $F_r=\mathcal H^r(C)$ with $r=2i-1$ or $2i$. If $(F_r)_{\bar y}\neq0$, then $r\leq\max(0,2h_y-2)$. Since $r>0$, this forces $h_y\geq i+1$ in either case. Step 2 therefore gives
$$e_y\leq d-i-1.$$
Consequently both $F_{2i-1}$ and $F_{2i}$ have the pointwise support-closure bound $s_i=d-i-1$. This statement uses geometric stalk support; it does not assume that this support is closed or constructible.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 5.3.2, printed pp. 288–289; Proposition 3.2.1, printed p. 268

proof.text:
Apply [lem-per-punctured-support-cohomological-bound] with $s=s_i$ to the sheaves killed by $\ell$ occurring below. To pass from those coefficients to $F_r$, use its finite filtration
$$F_r\supset\ell F_r\supset\cdots\supset\ell^nF_r=0.$$
Every quotient $Q_j=\ell^jF_r/\ell^{j+1}F_r$ is killed by $\ell$, and has zero stalk wherever $F_r$ has zero stalk, by exactness of stalks. Hence $H^p(U,Q_j)=0$ for $p\geq2s_i$. Each short exact sequence $0\to\ell^{j+1}F_r\to\ell^jF_r\to Q_j\to0$ gives a distinguished triangle. Derived global sections preserves these triangles: global sections is additive and left exact (it is a right adjoint), the sheaf category has enough injectives, and the cited bounded-below derived-functor theorem applies. The resulting long exact cohomology sequence, starting at $\ell^nF_r=0$ and descending in $j$, gives
$$H^p(U,F_r)=0\quad(p\geq2(d-i-1)).$$
No assertion that an injective module sheaf is injective as an abelian sheaf is used: all these triangles and derived global sections can be taken in abelian sheaves.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 5.3.2, printed pp. 288–289; Proposition 3.2.1, printed p. 268

proof.text:
We now use the finite ordinary truncation filtration of $C$, equivalently the finite filtration underlying the source's hypercohomology spectral sequence. Fix $t\geq2d-2$. If $r=2i-1$ or $2i$ with $1\leq i\leq d-2$, then
$$t-r\geq2(d-i-1),\qquad H^t(U,F_r[-r])=H^{t-r}(U,F_r)=0$$
by Step 4 and commutation of derived global sections with shifts. The successive-truncation triangle is
$$\tau_{\leq r-1}C\longrightarrow\tau_{\leq r}C\longrightarrow F_r[-r]\longrightarrow(\tau_{\leq r-1}C)[1].$$
Induct on $r$ from $\tau_{\leq0}C=0$ to $r=2d-4$: after derived global sections, the long exact sequence has zero outside terms $H^t(U,\tau_{\leq r-1}C)$ and $H^t(U,F_r[-r])$, so its middle term is zero. Since $C=\tau_{\leq2d-4}C$ in the derived category, this proves $H^t(U,C)=0$ for every $t\geq2d-2$. For $d=2$ the same conclusion follows directly from $C=0$, with no induction indices.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 5.3.2, printed pp. 288–289; Proposition 3.2.1, printed p. 268

proof.text:
For $q\geq2d$, apply derived global sections and the long exact cohomology sequence to the triangle of Step 1. Its segment is
$$H^{q-2}(U,C)\longrightarrow H^{q-1}(U,\Lambda)\xrightarrow{H^{q-1}(u)}H^{q-1}(U,M)\longrightarrow H^{q-1}(U,C).$$
Both outside groups vanish by Step 5, because $q-2\geq2d-2$. Exactness proves that the displayed map is an isomorphism, with the required specified $u$.

Hypotheses and the map u = truncation∘α match the source. Step 1: the ordinary truncation triangle, with α substituted. Step 2: h_y ≤ d−1 and h_y + e_y ≤ d by concatenating chains in the local X; stalks are exact and conservative, so H^r(C)=0 for r>2d−4; for d=2, C=0. Step 3: r ∈ {2i−1, 2i} forces e_y ≤ d−i−1, a correct arithmetic step. Step 4: filtration by powers of ℓ, then the new node on each ℓ-killed graded piece, with the ses-triangle, triangulated RΓ and long exact sequence nodes; the descending induction is set up correctly. Step 5: Postnikov induction from τ≤0C=0 up to 2d−4, using t−r ≥ 2(d−i−1). Step 6: the long exact sequence with both outer terms zero for q ≥ 2d. Every cited statement says what its step takes from it. New node lem-per-punctured-support-cohomological-bound: a faithful statement-only version of Prop 3.2.1, with the closure taken in X and no constructibility hypothesis. Small cases tested: s=0 (F=0); a surface point with constant F, where the bound is sharp at H^3; a height-one point (cd ≤ 1). It is not a restatement of the item. A DAG search turned up nearby nodes (the trf Gabber nearby-cycle and strict-local torsion bounds, thm-exc-curve-open-dimension-general, the qbar affine support bound) but no duplicate, and blueprint main-20261015 has none. Three Mathlib search kinds are recorded. I accept all six declared tool_uses as generic tools: the triangulated derived functor, the long exact sequence, the truncation triangle, stalk exactness, stalk conservativity (Lean-closed) and enough injectives. No SGA source is cited. No fixes.
